primitives.name: Dirichlet-Multinomial Target Share Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Target and carry *shares* are compositional (they sum to 1) and belong in a Dirichlet-multinomial, which gives negative teammate correlation, coherent same-game props, and turns injury re-projection into weight renormalization.
primitives.latex: \begin{aligned} \text{team_targets} &\sim \text{Binomial}(n = \text{dropbacks}, p = \text{script core}) \\ \text{target_shares} &\sim \text{DirichletMultinomial}(\boldsymbol{α}_1..\boldsymbol{α}_k) \quad (k = \text{active pass catchers}) \\ \boldsymbol{α}_i &= \exp\Bigl(β·\log(\text{est_route_share}_i) + \text{role covariates} + \text{QB effects} + \text{matchup effects}\Bigr) \end{aligned}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'n': 'Dimensionless (number)', 'p': 'Dimensionless (probability)', 'target_shares': 'Dimensionless (fraction of total targets)', 'α_i': 'Dimensionless (Dirichlet concentration parameter)', 'β': 'Dimensionless (coefficient)', 'log(est_route_share_i)': 'Dimensionless (natural logarithm of estimated route share)', 'role covariates': 'Dimensionless (categorical or numeric encoding)', 'QB effects': 'Dimensionless (quality-adjusted quarterback contribution)', 'matchup effects': 'Dimensionless (opponent-specific adjustment)'}
primitives.assumptions: Compositional data summing to 1, multinomial trials conditional on total targets, Dirichlet prior over share probabilities with fixed-effects linear predictor, hierarchical partial pooling across players and positions.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a receiver is inactive (zero targets), the model automatically renormalizes shares while maintaining negative correlation with remaining teammates; extreme overdispersion occurs when the Dirichlet concentration parameter approaches zero.

primitives.name: Quantile Settlement for Skewed Props
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Props are quantile bets, not mean bets.** A line at 62.5 receiving yards settles on a quantile of a right-skewed mixture, not on a mean.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E[Y | Y > 0]': 'Yards (mean receiving yards given positive output)', 'y': 'Yards (individual outcome)', 'f(y)': 'Probability density function', 'P(Y > 62.5)': 'Dimensionless (probability of exceeding 62.5 yards)'}
primitives.assumptions: The distribution of receiving yards is right-skewed with a mass point at zero (due to non-participation), and the book's line is set at a quantile of this mixture distribution rather than the arithmetic mean.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When the underlying distribution becomes highly skewed or censored (e.g., blowouts leading to benchings), using the mean as a settlement rule introduces bias; the quantile formulation correctly captures the tail behavior relevant to betting.
